paper_summary: Phenolic (resol, in-situ synthesized) syntactic foams with 10-40 wt% hollow glass microspheres (0.3-0.6 g/cm3, 30-100 um) were made by stirring, hot compaction at 180 C/4 MPa/60 min and curing at 150 C. Density, tensile and compressive strength decreased with microsphere content while tensile modulus increased; 40 wt% showed extensive microsphere crushing. Thermal conductivity fell from 0.298 W/mK (neat) to a minimum of 0.129 W/mK at 20 wt% and TGA char yield at 700 C rose from 59.3% to 78.0%.

extraction_notes: Only thermal conductivity (Table 3) and TGA data (Table 2, put in microstructure_notes) are reported numerically. Densities (Fig. 2), tensile strength/modulus (Fig. 5) and compressive strength/modulus (Fig. 6) appear only as bar charts with no numbers in text, so all mechanical fields are left null; test conditions were ISO 527 tension (2 mm/min, 100x10x4 mm) and ISO 604 compression (25 mm cubes, 2 mm/min, to 10 mm deflection). Neat resin (0 wt%) included as a baseline record. Particle density/diameter given only as ranges (0.3-0.6 g/cm3, 30-100 um) so left null. cure_or_process_temperature_c = 180 C hot-press; post-cure 10-15 h at 150 C. test_type=other denotes thermal conductivity measurement.
